record.paper_title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems
record.original_question: How can a tensegrity framework be designed by generating a new topology, including which nodes are connected, which kind of edge is used for each connection, the spatial nodal configuration, and the edge stresses, so that the resulting structure achieves a desired performance criterion such as stiffness, stiffness-to-mass ratio, or deformation under external forces while satisfying the geometrical and statical constraints required for a feasible tensegrity realization?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tensegrity framework consists of a finite set of nodes $V = \{p_1, \ldots, p_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d \in \{2,3\}$) together with a set of edges $E$, where each edge $e \in E$ is labeled as either a cable (which can only sustain tensile axial force, i.e., stress $\sigma_e \ge 0$) or a strut (which can only sustain compressive axial force, $\sigma_e \le 0$). A self-equilibrated tensegrity realization is a quadruple $(V, E, \tau, \sigma)$, where $\tau: E \to \{\text{cable}, \text{strut}\}$ is the edge-type assignment and $\sigma: E \to \mathbb{R}$ is a stress assignment, satisfying:
(i) Static equilibrium at every node in the absence of external load: for each node $p_i$, $\sum_{e=\{i,j\} \in E} \sigma_e (p_j - p_i) = 0$.
(ii) Sign feasibility: $\sigma_e \ge 0$ if $\tau(e) = \text{cable}$ and $\sigma_e \le 0$ if $\tau(e) = \text{strut}$.
(iii) Prestress stability: the tangent stiffness matrix $K(V,E,\sigma) = K_E + K_G$ (sum of elastic and geometric stiffness matrices) is positive semidefinite, with kernel consisting only of rigid-body motions.

Given a design domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, a candidate node set or generation rule, a maximum number of nodes/edges, and a performance functional $\mathcal{P}$ (for example, overall stiffness with respect to a prescribed load, the stiffness-to-mass ratio, or the maximum deformation under a specified external load case), provide a constructive procedure that simultaneously determines:
(a) the connectivity pattern (which pairs of nodes are joined by an edge),
(b) the edge-type labeling $\tau$ for each edge (cable or strut),
(c) the spatial nodal positions $\{p_i\} \subset \Omega$, and
(d) a feasible self-stress $\sigma$,
so that the resulting tensegrity realization satisfies conditions (i)–(iii) and optimizes the performance functional $\mathcal{P}$.

Formulate and solve this combined topology, geometry, and prestress design problem for general performance criteria, beyond the case of a fixed pre-specified topology where only $\sigma$ and node positions are computed.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature treats this as an active, largely open challenge. Most established form-finding methods assume a given topology and solve only for nodal coordinates and self-stresses; jointly generating topology, edge types, geometry, and prestress for arbitrary performance criteria remains under active investigation, with recent partial advances via mixed-integer programming, rank-constrained LMIs, and scheme-matrix algorithms but no general solution.

status_evidence.title: A unifying framework for form-finding and topology-finding of tensegrity structures
status_evidence.snippet: Despite numerous studies on form-finding... seldom work until now has investigated the extension of form-finding methods to topology-finding of tensegrity structures.
status_evidence.claim: Joint topology-and-form finding remains a recently developed and incomplete research direction.

status_evidence.title: Topology optimization of tensegrity structures under compliance constraint
status_evidence.snippet: Topology optimization problems of tensegrity structures under compliance constraint via mixed integer linear programming.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists via topology optimization for specific compliance/stiffness criteria.

status_evidence.title: Topological form-finding analysis of regular tensegrity structure based on parallel component coding algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Significant challenges remain in addressing the topological form-finding problem associated with regular tensegrity structures that exhibit multiple self-stress modes.
status_evidence.claim: Authors explicitly state significant open challenges remain in the topological form-finding problem.
